basis: Source semantics plus separately retained host capability/clock query evidence; no game latency measurement

signals.update_rule: Increment/decrement at attached generic hardirq-action and softirq handler boundaries; event driven.
signals.clock_or_units: Counter; observer timestamps only if added.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Own CPU writes; remote load can race. Generic IRQ actions do not cover all APIC/NMI/firmware work. Missing attachment is not quiet.
signals.access_and_cost: Already in Cake: BPF entry/exit execution plus one padded-slot read; cache coherence cost unmeasured.
signals.cake_use: Refine candidate choice; compare broader kernel snapshot against current writer cost.
signals.invalidation: Attach/detach, nesting, CPU lifecycle, coverage change.

signals.update_rule: At architecture vector entry/exit; no fixed publication period.
signals.clock_or_units: Trace clock or BPF observation clock.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Earlier boundary than a generic device action, different coverage. Avoid double-counting nested intervals.
signals.access_and_cost: Trace events available; extra observers cost per vector. Production summary would need kernel ownership.
signals.cake_use: Identify missing interference; fold into a bounded candidate hint only if beneficial.
signals.invalidation: Architecture/config, nested IRQ, detach/hotplug.

signals.update_rule: Accumulates at IRQ accounting boundaries, including entry/exit; running interval may not yet be charged.
signals.clock_or_units: Duration ns derived from sched_clock_cpu; not a MONOTONIC epoch timestamp.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Fine units; excludes ksoftirqd task execution. Requires enabled accounting and coherent reads; no hard maximum publication lag.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing internal counter; proposed bounded kfunc, no text parse. No measured reader/writer ns cost.
signals.cake_use: Short-window CPU interference estimate without adding a new time source to every event.
signals.invalidation: Availability, CPU online generation, baseline for counter differences.

signals.update_rule: One-second loop; sampling adapts to 1–4 seconds; mark/unmark requires 2/3 confirming windows.
signals.clock_or_units: USER_HZ ticks; host CLK_TCK=100, 10 ms units.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Slow aggregate intentionally hysteretic; interval is not a guaranteed freshness bound if loader is delayed.
signals.access_and_cost: Text parsing/cold userspace update; BPF reads cached mask.
signals.cake_use: Chronic interference only; keep distinct from immediate handler depth.
signals.invalidation: CPU topology, unknown samples, process stalls, attachment generation.

signals.update_rule: Core changes rq->curr on scheduling transition; query reads current pointer.
signals.clock_or_units: Identity/state, not a timestamp.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: RCU protects lifetime, not a stable occupant or a reserved CPU. IRQ can execute while the interrupted task remains curr.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing kfunc/compat wrapper; candidate-local remote read. No need to poll through userspace.
signals.cake_use: Observe occupant/RT interference while keeping authoritative idle claims.
signals.invalidation: Context switch, migration, task exit, CPU hotplug.

signals.update_rule: Cached after rq clock update until rq unpin/unlock invalidates; otherwise fresh sched_clock_cpu read.
signals.clock_or_units: ns; scheduler clock family, same-CPU ordering only.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Repeated calls can return identical values; cross-CPU deltas may be negative. Not interchangeable with MONOTONIC.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing fast kfunc. Cache savings trade timestamp freshness; no cost measured here.
signals.cake_use: Existing internal accounting; exclude from external GPU/input timestamp joins.
signals.invalidation: CPU provenance, cache validity, clocksource/suspend events.

signals.update_rule: Read on call; kernel timekeeping supplies current clock conversion.
signals.clock_or_units: CLOCK_MONOTONIC ns; implementation uses mono_fast accessor.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Host reports 1 ns resolution, not accuracy. Frequency discipline applies; suspend excluded; fast accessor has exceptional timekeeping caveats.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing BPF helper; reuse event timestamp rather than repeat reads. No measured BPF read latency here.
signals.cake_use: Common domain for readiness/publication/consumption timestamps.
signals.invalidation: Boot/session generation; reject impossible negative/outlier deltas rather than silently counting zero.

signals.update_rule: jiffies-based approximation with offset measured at Cake attach; host coarse resolution is 1 ms.
signals.clock_or_units: jiffies * nominal tick + one-time MONOTONIC offset.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Lifetime approximation only; tick quantization, NO_HZ batching and calibration mean it is not an exact cross-component clock.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing cheap cached conversion; fallback precise read when tick rejected.
signals.cake_use: Keep for its documented age use; never repurpose for device/deadline measurements.
signals.invalidation: Attach, suspend/clock changes; long-duration error has not been characterized.

signals.update_rule: Updated by scheduler execution accounting; current running segment may be pending until accounting runs.
signals.clock_or_units: Accumulated service ns, not wall-clock epoch.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: IRQ/steal subtraction belongs to kernel accounting. Runtime does not reveal frame completion or wall-clock waiting.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing task field read; lifetime and concurrent updates matter.
signals.cake_use: Keep service budgets separate from readiness age and wall time.
signals.invalidation: Task lifetime, last accounting update; never subtract IRQ twice.

signals.update_rule: Event-driven during successful wake path; waking precedes normal CPU choice, wakeup occurs later.
signals.clock_or_units: No intrinsic timestamp in state; use the chosen observer clock.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Reason absent; some paths skip select_cpu and already-runnable events need no wake. Current PID in IRQ is not cause ownership.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing callback receives actual task; new typed metadata can ride existing wake with no daemon round trip.
signals.cake_use: Read cause before first placement, and handle enqueue/next service where selection is skipped.
signals.invalidation: Task/dependency generation, duplicate/failed wakes, concurrent causes.

signals.signal: Task selected, running, preempted or blocked
signals.update_rule: At scheduling transitions; Cake receives its class callbacks. All-class sched_switch covers RT as well.
signals.clock_or_units: Timestamp at callback/switch boundary; execution-accounting clock is distinct.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: running/sched_switch precede actual application resume. stopping can mean preempted, not blocked or done.
signals.access_and_cost: Reuse Cake notifications; trace observer only for other classes/research.
signals.cake_use: Maintain scheduling state without an extra cross-process state query.
signals.invalidation: Migration, class change, CPU hotplug, task exit; record transition generation.

signals.update_rule: Kfunc reads arch_scale_freq_capacity; x86 reference updates scale from APERF/MPERF intervals on tick path.
signals.clock_or_units: Normalized capacity, not instantaneous GHz or a timestamp.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Host HZ=1000 is nominal active tick cadence; NO_HZ/idle/disabled invariance can leave older/default scale. No general 1 ms freshness guarantee.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing kfunc; recomputing ratios or polling cpufreq in BPF would duplicate work.
signals.cake_use: Optional candidate service-capacity hint, only if it improves choices.
signals.invalidation: Architecture path, active sampling, CPU topology/power state.

signals.update_rule: clock_event_device next_event changes when timer programming changes.
signals.clock_or_units: ktime/MONOTONIC deadline.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Advisory remote snapshot; not all future interrupts, not necessarily a periodic scheduler tick, and hardware may fire late.
signals.access_and_cost: Cake already uses weak tick_cpu_device symbol and one search clock read.
signals.cake_use: Predict a nearby programmed event without broad timer polling.
signals.invalidation: Reprogramming, tick stop, device replacement, suspend/hotplug.

signals.update_rule: GPU semaphore advances with submitted work; RM/KAPI notification invokes registered callback; DRM then reads sequence.
signals.clock_or_units: Timeline sequence, not calibrated CPU timestamp.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Source code does not bound GPU completion-to-RM callback latency. Context/timeline scope matters; one device-wide bit loses attribution.
signals.access_and_cost: Driver-owned mapping and callbacks; not an arbitrary BPF-loadable GPU pointer.
signals.cake_use: Publish known dependency progress on existing callback; avoid MMIO/RM polling in Cake.
signals.invalidation: Sequence/context lifetime, 32/64-bit expansion, reset/error, submission generation.

signals.update_rule: One successful signal per fence; flag, tracepoint, timestamp publication, then callbacks in source order.
signals.clock_or_units: Supplied timestamp must be CLOCK_MONOTONIC; ordinary signal samples ktime_get.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Signaled tracepoint precedes timestamp-union publication. Ordinary NVIDIA signal timestamp is software delivery time, not exact hardware finish.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing trace/function argument; add typed metadata only under correct lifetime/atomic-context rules.
signals.cake_use: Carry completion/error cause to actual waiter before CPU placement.
signals.invalidation: Fence context+seqno+generation; errors, chains/arrays, timeout/reuse.

signals.update_rule: Registered callback runs when dependency signals, then calls existing task wake.
signals.clock_or_units: Timestamp at satisfied wait; common MONOTONIC observation recommended.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Actual waiter known, but only these wait implementations are covered. Wake acceptance and first service are later distinct events.
signals.access_and_cost: Direct kernel path; proposed cause handoff need not add userspace or a workqueue.
signals.cake_use: High-priority candidate for precise ready-to-CPU attribution.
signals.invalidation: Timeout/cancel, callback removal, task lifetime, merged waits.

signals.update_rule: Availability updates when fence for a point is installed; completion updates only when it signals.
signals.clock_or_units: Sequence/flags; these are different logical events.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: WAIT_AVAILABLE can wake while GPU work is unfinished. One generic GPU-ready label is incorrect.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing wait flag/point registration; timestamp and type must travel together.
signals.cake_use: Learn future dependency early, but mark runnable-for-dependent-work only at the required stage.
signals.invalidation: Timeline point and flags, replacement, context reset, chained fences.

signals.update_rule: Completion callback signals eventfd; availability-only mode can signal earlier; epoll queues readiness and wakes waiters.
signals.clock_or_units: Observer timestamps; object has no universal frame clock.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Fan-in/coalescing/already-readable eventfd break one-event/one-wake assumptions; mode must be preserved.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing kernel notification, then consumer service. Metadata propagation needs a valid identity across aggregation.
signals.cake_use: Measure queue boundary and preserve cause into actual consumer.
signals.invalidation: FD/object lifetime, point/mode, readiness consumption, epoll fan-out.

signals.update_rule: Poll installs callback if needed; signaled fence wakes waitqueue and yields EPOLLIN.
signals.clock_or_units: Fence state plus observation clock.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Observer registration may enable software signaling. Actual consumer can be epoll, not direct CPU fence waiter.
signals.access_and_cost: Callback+waitqueue; avoid assuming poll wake implies a new task transition.
signals.cake_use: Cover alternative GPU-to-compositor route without misattributing by submitting PID.
signals.invalidation: File/fence lifetime, callback registration, shared waiters.

signals.update_rule: Fence callback queues worker when RM operation cannot run in interrupt context; already-signaled ioctl has immediate path.
signals.clock_or_units: Record enqueue/start/end in one CPU clock domain.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Queue latency is workload-dependent; source gives no maximum. Must identify actual required worker and class.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing workqueue boundary; no gain from boosting an unrelated game thread.
signals.cake_use: Measure and prioritize real runnable dependency, or redesign safe deferral if justified.
signals.invalidation: Worker/context teardown, retry/error, dependency generation.

signals.update_rule: Successful wake-mark adds actual task to wake_q; wake follows lock release.
signals.clock_or_units: Logical wake plus chosen clock; ordinary futex has no general owner contract.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Timeout/racing wakes and PI semantics matter; user word is not a trusted task pointer.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing wake path; cause must survive wake_q and deduplication.
signals.cake_use: Shorten proven dependency handoffs, not all short-sleeping threads.
signals.invalidation: Wait-key reuse, requeue, cancel, duplicate wake and task lifetime.

signals.update_rule: Object updates evaluate wait conditions and atomically satisfy a wait before waking q->task.
signals.clock_or_units: Logical readiness; annotate monotonic time if needed.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Owner field is opaque userspace ID; all-wait readiness is not each individual object being signaled at some earlier time.
signals.access_and_cost: Driver knows waiter; typed wake must preserve its existing lock/context ordering.
signals.cake_use: Potential Proton path after verifying title usage; precise readiness beats ioctl-name heuristics.
signals.invalidation: Object/instance/task lifetime, owner mismatch, alert/timeout/cancel.

signals.update_rule: Driver supplies event time, or input core samples ktime_get when no valid timestamp exists; reset on flush.
signals.clock_or_units: MONOTONIC internally; REALTIME/BOOTTIME conversions also stored.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: May be receipt timestamp; no guaranteed physical sensor timestamp. Delayed conversion across suspend can be inaccurate.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing event time; observe producer field, not a later clock read mislabeled as hardware time.
signals.cake_use: Input age with source-quality flag and consumer identity.
signals.invalidation: Device/report generation, suspend, synthetic events and clock choice.

signals.update_rule: Successful USB URB completion processes report; cadence depends on device/USB configuration and generated reports.
signals.clock_or_units: Receipt observation time, not physical scan time.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: 1/8 kHz imply 1 ms/125 us nominal intervals only as examples; this device cadence is not measured.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing driver function; tracing every event has cost. BPF cannot eliminate pre-arrival firmware/USB time.
signals.cake_use: Locate upstream delay; do not wake an unrouted consumer before packet readiness.
signals.invalidation: Disconnect/reset, report parsing errors, HID quirks, transport.

signals.update_rule: Nonempty SYN_REPORT packet publication, then poll wake after client buffer lock is released.
signals.clock_or_units: Selected evdev clock; serialized timeval truncates ns to microseconds.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Up to <1 us serialization truncation, plus earlier timestamp uncertainty and later queue delay. Clock changes can flush pending data/SYN_DROPPED.
signals.access_and_cost: Actual evdev client context known; trace or typed notification at readiness, no raw key/coordinate payload needed.
signals.cake_use: Good generic input cause origin before downstream epoll/task selection.
signals.invalidation: Client grab/revoke, SYN_DROPPED, clock switch, device/task lifetimes.

signals.update_rule: KWin dispatches and queues libinput events when its event-loop service runs; empty-to-nonempty emits notification.
signals.clock_or_units: libinput MONOTONIC microseconds; arrival order need not match event timestamp order.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Timestamp can retain event age despite delayed delivery; synthesized events can have older timestamps.
signals.access_and_cost: Userspace event queue; kernel cannot infer route through Qt without cooperation or measured association.
signals.cake_use: Separate event age, queue age and freshest sample age.
signals.invalidation: Seat/device/focus and process generation; synthesized-event semantics.

signals.update_rule: Queued Qt notification, processed on main-thread service; consecutive motion events coalesced with latest event time.
signals.clock_or_units: Event time in MONOTONIC us; add enqueue/dequeue stamps separately.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Unbounded under stalls; latest-only timestamp hides oldest backlog. Both involved host threads are RR priority 1.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing userspace handoff; preserve dependency metadata rather than add another polling broker.
signals.cake_use: Measure this queue separately from Cake-owned game CPU queue.
signals.invalidation: Consumer acknowledgment, focus, suspend and process lifetime.

signals.update_rule: Per accepted input edge/report; kernel or higher layers may generate repeat.
signals.clock_or_units: Event MONOTONIC us in KWin; event class determines meaning.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Press/release ordering and seat counts matter. Repeat is not a new hardware scan; release lag needs its own measurement.
signals.access_and_cost: Reuse packet readiness with discrete-input class; no keycode required for scheduler.
signals.cake_use: Bound urgency until real consumer handles edge; do not renew forever on repeat.
signals.invalidation: Focus loss, dropped synchronization, held-key state, disconnect, acknowledgment.

signals.signal: KWin acquire fence to transaction readiness
signals.update_rule: KWin requests eventfd with flags=0 for acquire point; unreadable fd becomes a transaction fence and event-loop dependency.
signals.clock_or_units: Timeline point is completion state; event-loop notification time is later.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Source path waits for completion, distinct from isMaterialized WAIT_AVAILABLE. Whether game uses this path is not traced yet.
signals.access_and_cost: GPU fence -> kernel eventfd -> KWin event loop; per-point setup exists already.
signals.cake_use: Concrete compositor consumer route worth measuring; main thread remains RT.
signals.invalidation: Surface/transaction/point generation, fence error/discard, client exit.

signals.signal: KWin planned frame and render start
signals.update_rule: Recomputed when scheduling/revising repaint; render estimate updated after frame feedback.
signals.clock_or_units: steady_clock ns; current Linux presentation clock verified MONOTONIC; timer duration is cast to ms.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Prediction, not measured future time. 1 ms extra safety allowance and sub-ms timer conversion affect planning; VRR/queue state change it.
signals.access_and_cost: Userspace already owns frame target; proposed bounded phase/target publication.
signals.cake_use: Advisory latest-start/slack for actual dependency; no permanent process priority.
signals.invalidation: Frame/output generation, refresh/VRR/mode change, estimate age, suspend.

signals.update_rule: Optional callback stores supplied timestamp per vblank; read uses cache to avoid sleeping KAPI call under DRM locks.
signals.clock_or_units: Driver-supplied ns timestamp; end-to-end hardware origin not established here.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Host nvidia_drm.vblank=N: this optional path is disabled. Available symbols alone do not make it live; separate pageflip feedback can still work.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing kernel cache if enabled; do not enable as part of observation or infer absent feedback from this flag alone.
signals.cake_use: Output phase evidence only after coverage/clock validation; vblank is not per-game completion.
signals.invalidation: Enablement, output/mode lifecycle, last-event age, fallback quality.

signals.update_rule: Feedback per requested surface content update after presentation or discard; delivery may lag embedded event timestamp.
signals.clock_or_units: Advertised presentation clock: host CLOCK_MONOTONIC; seconds+ns plus quality flags.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: HW_CLOCK/HW_COMPLETION/ZERO_COPY flags have distinct meanings. Buffer release can occur without display; protocol availability does not prove a game's coverage.
signals.access_and_cost: Existing Wayland protocol; CPU scheduler needs cooperative frame association, not direct protocol parsing in BPF.
signals.cake_use: Outcome validation and prediction calibration, not a future-ready fact.
signals.invalidation: Connection clock, output, frame ID, discard, mode/VRR and buffer generation.

signals.update_rule: If supported and subscribed, accompanies next matching timestamped input event.
signals.clock_or_units: seconds+ns in same domain as corresponding input timestamp.
signals.accuracy_and_staleness: Higher representation precision does not recover precision already lost upstream. Not advertised in this host registry snapshot.
signals.access_and_cost: Userspace protocol; availability must be negotiated, not inferred from installed XML.
signals.cake_use: Optional measurement/phase publisher input, not a required Cake dependency.
signals.invalidation: Seat subscription, device/client lifetime, clock mapping and event matching.
